perez_zeledon.description: Discover the history of the canton, some curiosities, its districts and all the beauties found in them
perez_zeledon.districts_description: Pérez Zeledón currently divides its territory into 12 districts. Enjoy the beauties that each one of them has
perez_zeledon.history_description: A brief tour of the canton's history
perez_zeledon.origin_description: At the end of the nineteenth century, between 1870 and 1899, there were already several families living in Valle del General. Firstly, El General and Palmares became more seriously populated from 1900. Then, Rivas and Ureña were populated in 1911, especially Ureña that had a faster growth during the administration of Ricardo Jimenez Oreamuno. The shelters of Ojo de agua, Cerro de la Muerte, and División were also built, which served both the pioneers and founders of Pérez Zeledón in later years.
perez_zeledon.education_description: With the benefit of the shelters and the cabotage service, which reached Dominical and Uvita beach, the transfer to the center of the country and vice versa was greatly favored. In addition, the way of taking and bringing crops, products and articles of urgent need, and of course the influx of new inhabitants was greater. During the second administration of Ricardo Jiménez Oreamuno, the first teachers paid by the State, nine women and two men, arrived in Valle del General (Manuel Monge Zúñiga and Cornelio Martínez had already worked voluntarily in El General, Palmares and Ureña) who distributed in the few existing populations.
perez_zeledon.we_are_canton_description: With this educational awakening, the inhabitants began a movement to convince the doteños to accept the separation, which led to the founding of the canton number nineteen of the province of San José. It was founded by decree number thirty-one of October 9, 1931., with the name of Pérez Zeledón, a character recognized by Costa Rican history as one of its great men.
perez_zeledon.the_first_municipality_description: Now with a good quality of life in the canton, the Principal Police Agent, Mr. Trinidad Montero Rodríguez, became Political Chief and therefore Municipal Executive. He had the honor of swearing in the first municipality on Sunday, January 1, 1932, which was composed and formed to hold meetings the same day in the presence of the inhabitants, who applauded happy to have reached the cantonate and start a greater fight for the progress and development of the new and thriving Canton.
perez_zeledon.the_canton_continues_to_grow_description: Later, with the arrival of the National Radio Office, the postal service, the aviation service, and the major construction work of the Inter-American highway (1936 - 1945) with machinery that entered through Cartago and Dominical, the development was truly remarkable, and the canton began to receive inhabitants from almost all regions of the country, especially teachers who fought together with the towns for greater progress and general well-being.
perez_zeledon.biodiversity_description1: Pérez Zeledón has an extension of 1905.51 kilometers. Part of this canton is located in the vicinity of the South Pacific and near the Talamanca Mountain Range. Due to its great extension, there are four hydrographic basins in the canton: Savegre, Barú, Higuerón, and General. These hydrographic basins give a broken relief and many water tributaries that separate the landscape. The tributaries of these basins and the marked volcanic activity in previous millennia contribute to the canton's territory having a marked altitudinal gradient, with areas below 400 meters above sea level. and including the highest peak in the country, the Chirripó with 3820 meters above sea level.
perez_zeledon.biodiversity_description2: Due to the geomorphology and the influence of the ocean currents with their winds, the canton has nine life zones according to Holdridge's classification, and four transition zones. The most popular ones that predominate are the premontane very humid forest, the premontane rainforest, and the lower montane rain forest. Due to its large size and life zones, it provides an ideal site for the development of various agricultural activities, as well as a great biodiversity of native wild species.
perez_zeledon.biodiversity_description3: Perez Zeledon is famous for ornithological tourism and the sighting of 518 species of birds has been reported. This number becomes relevant when considering that 923 species are seen in the whole country, with November to March being the best time to observe migratory species. Mammals are not far behind and approximately 70 species of bats are reported, out of the 118 registered for the country, as well as approximately 54 species of rodents. Apart from rodents and bats, there are 41 species of mammals from casual to common sightings, which include three of the four species of monkeys in the country (Howler monkey, Cebus capucinus which has a white face, and Ateles geoffroyi), two species of sloths (Choloepus hoffmani that has two fingers and Bradypus variegatus that has three fingers), tapirs, and six species of wild cats in the country.
perez_zeledon.biodiversity_description4: Unlike mammals and birds, which have great diversity in most of the canton, people can find a high diversity of amphibians and reptiles in the lowlands. Approximately 43 species of frogs and toads have been recorded, as well as 35 species of lizards and geckos. Snakes excel in this diversity although they are organisms with unusual sightings. Snakes also contribute a great biodiversity to the canton with approximately 40 species, but only seven of them are of medical importance.
perez_zeledon.biodiversity_description5: (Important note: the information collected was obtained from field guides and censuses carried out in regions within or that included territory of the canton; however, there are no diversity studies at the canton or district level. For this reason, the numbers of Species listed are reliable approximations and sightings. Some numbers may change as the taxonomy of the groups is updated).
perez_zeledon.biodiversity_credits: By Keneth Barrantes Fallas, UCR Biologist.
perez_zeledon.geological_features_description: This canton is geologically formed by classic Oligocene marine deposits, mainly Miocene intrusive rocks, including quartz, diorite, and to a lesser extent granite and gabbro. Lastly, classical and contemporary marine deposits (Terraces) from the Pleistocene. Pérez Zeledón has a fairly broken surface, having 90% of its surface with slopes greater than 6%, the limit between what is considered flat and slightly undulating terrain. Only 6% of the area of ​​the canton has a flat surface, and 4% is slightly undulating, while the surface that is greater than 30% represents 56% of the entire canton.
perez_zeledon.geological_features_credits: Instituto de Desarrollo Rural, (2016). Caracterización del Territorio Pérez Zeledón. Pérez Zeledón, pp.36.
perez_zeledon.geographic_location_description: Pérez Zeledón is located in the south of the country. The maximum width is 68 kilometers in the northwest to southeast direction, from the border with the Aguirre canton, over the Savegre River to the confluence of the Caliente River with the Guácima ravine. The extension of Pérez Zeledón is 1905.51 square kilometers, which represents 38.42% of the territory of the San José province and in turn 3.33% of the National Territory. The main city, San Isidro de El General, is located 136 kilometers from San José, the capital of Costa Rica. It limits to the north with the cantons of Paraíso, Jiménez, Turrialba and part of Dota; to the south with the canton of Osa, to the east with the cantons of Limón, Talamanca, and Buenos Aires, and to the west with the cantons of Aguirre and part of Dota.
perez_zeledon.flora_and_fauna_description: Thanks to the different Forest Reserves and the Chirripó National Park there are some species that are located in the territory. For example, there are different kinds of birds, which are the following: Thraupis episcopus, Pitangus sulphuratus, Columbina talpacoti, Zonotrichia capensis, Quiscalus nicaraguensis, Coragyps atratus, and Caracara cheriway. Other species found in secondary forests to a lesser degree are Agelaius phoeniceus, Molothrus aeneus, Melanerpes rubricapillus, Tangara icterocephala, Passerina ciristoucanet, Aulacorhynchus prasinus, Capsiempis flaveola, Manacus aurantiacus,Tyrannus savana, among others. The amphibians that can be observed are Agalychnis callidryas, snakes such as Bothrops asper, Bothriechis schlegelii, Boa constrictor, Oxybelis aeneus, among others. Within the lizards you can see Iguana iguana, Ctenosaura similis, and Aspidoscelis deppei. The El General Valley has a unique floristic composition in the country. The most common species of flora that can be found in Valle del General are: Brosimum utile, Virola koschnyi, Bactris gasipaes, Eriobotrya japonica, and Samanea saman.  In addition, Roystonea borinquena, Cassia grandis, Samanea saman, Pseudobombax septenatum, Ochroma pyramidale, and Platymiscium pleiostachyum can also be observed.
perez_zeledon.flora_and_fauna_credits: Instituto de Desarrollo Rural, (2016). Caracterización del Territorio Pérez Zeledón. Pérez Zeledón, pp.37.
